paragraphs.text: translated by
1. Go hence, O Death, pursue thy special pathway apart from that which Gods are wont to travel.
paragraphs.original: परं मृत्यो अनु परेहि पन्थां यस्ते स्व इतरो देवयानात् ।
paragraphs.translit: paraṃ mṛtyo anu parehi panthāṃ yaste sva itaro devayānāt |

paragraphs.text: To thee I say it who hast eyes and hearest: Touch not our offspring, injure not our heroes.
paragraphs.original: चक्षुष्मते शृण्वते ते ब्रवीमि मा नः प्रजां रीरिषो मोत वीरान्
paragraphs.translit: cakṣuṣmate śṛṇvate te bravīmi mā naḥ prajāṃ rīriṣo mota vīrān

paragraphs.text: 2. As ye have come effacing Mrtyu's footstep, to further times prolonging your existence,
paragraphs.original: मृत्योः पदं योपयन्तो यदैत द्राघीय आयुः प्रतरं दधानाः ।
paragraphs.translit: mṛtyoḥ padaṃ yopayanto yadaita drāghīya āyuḥ prataraṃ dadhānāḥ |

paragraphs.text: May ye be rich in children and possessions. cleansed, purified, and meet for sacrificing.
paragraphs.original: आप्यायमानाः प्रजया धनेन शुद्धाः पूता भवत यज्ञियासः
paragraphs.translit: āpyāyamānāḥ prajayā dhanena śuddhāḥ pūtā bhavata yajñiyāsaḥ

paragraphs.text: 3. Divided from the dead are these, the living: now be our calling on the Gods successful.
paragraphs.original: इमे जीवा वि मृतैराववृत्रन्नभूद्भद्रा देवहूतिर्नो अद्य ।
paragraphs.translit: ime jīvā vi mṛtairāvavṛtrannabhūdbhadrā devahūtirno adya |

paragraphs.text: We have gone forth for dancing and for laughter, to further times prolonging our existence.
paragraphs.original: प्राञ्चो अगाम नृतये हसाय द्राघीय आयुः प्रतरं दधानाः
paragraphs.translit: prāñco agāma nṛtaye hasāya drāghīya āyuḥ prataraṃ dadhānāḥ

paragraphs.text: 4. Here I erect this rampart for the living; let none of these, none other, reach this limit.
paragraphs.original: इमं जीवेभ्यः परिधिं दधामि मैषां नु गादपरो अर्थमेतम् ।
paragraphs.translit: imaṃ jīvebhyaḥ paridhiṃ dadhāmi maiṣāṃ nu gādaparo arthametam |

paragraphs.text: May they survive a hundred lengthened autumns, and may they bury Death beneath this mountain.
paragraphs.original: शतं जीवन्तु शरदः पुरूचीरन्तर्मृत्युं दधतां पर्वतेन
paragraphs.translit: śataṃ jīvantu śaradaḥ purūcīrantarmṛtyuṃ dadhatāṃ parvatena

paragraphs.text: 5. As the days follow days in close succession, as with the seasons duly come the seasons,
paragraphs.original: यथाहान्यनुपूर्वं भवन्ति यथ ऋतव ऋतुभिर्यन्ति साधु ।
paragraphs.translit: yathāhānyanupūrvaṃ bhavanti yatha ṛtava ṛtubhiryanti sādhu |

paragraphs.text: As each successor fails not his foregoer, so form the lives of these, O great Ordainer.
paragraphs.original: यथा न पूर्वमपरो जहात्येवा धातरायूंषि कल्पयैषाम्
paragraphs.translit: yathā na pūrvamaparo jahātyevā dhātarāyūṃṣi kalpayaiṣām

paragraphs.text: 6. Live your full lives up! find old age delightful, all of you striving one behind the other.
paragraphs.original: आ रोहतायुर्जरसं वृणाना अनुपूर्वं यतमाना यति ष्ठ ।
paragraphs.translit: ā rohatāyurjarasaṃ vṛṇānā anupūrvaṃ yatamānā yati ṣṭha |

paragraphs.text: May Tvastar, maker of fair things, be gracious and lengthen out the days of your existence.
paragraphs.original: इह त्वष्टा सुजनिमा सजोषा दीर्घमायुः करति जीवसे वः
paragraphs.translit: iha tvaṣṭā sujanimā sajoṣā dīrghamāyuḥ karati jīvase vaḥ

paragraphs.text: 7. Let these unwidowed dames with noble husbands adorn themselves with fragrant balm and unguent.
paragraphs.original: इमा नारीरविधवाः सुपत्नीराञ्जनेन सर्पिषा सं विशन्तु ।
paragraphs.translit: imā nārīravidhavāḥ supatnīrāñjanena sarpiṣā saṃ viśantu |

paragraphs.text: Decked with fair jewels, tearless, free from sorrow, first let the dames go up to where he lieth.
paragraphs.original: अनश्रवोऽनमीवाः सुरत्ना आ रोहन्तु जनयो योनिमग्रे
paragraphs.translit: anaśravo'namīvāḥ suratnā ā rohantu janayo yonimagre

paragraphs.text: 8. Rise, come unto the world of life, O woman: come, he is lifeless by whose side thou liest.
paragraphs.original: उदीर्ष्व नार्यभि जीवलोकं गतासुमेतमुप शेष एहि ।
paragraphs.translit: udīrṣva nāryabhi jīvalokaṃ gatāsumetamupa śeṣa ehi |

paragraphs.text: Wifehood with this thy husband was thy portion, who took thy hand and wooed thee as a lover.
paragraphs.original: हस्तग्राभस्य दिधिषोस्तवेदं पत्युर्जनित्वमभि सं बभूथ
paragraphs.translit: hastagrābhasya didhiṣostavedaṃ patyurjanitvamabhi saṃ babhūtha

paragraphs.text: 9. From his dead hand I take the bow be carried, that it may be our power and might and glory.
paragraphs.original: धनुर्हस्तादाददानो मृतस्यास्मे क्षत्राय वर्चसे बलाय ।
paragraphs.translit: dhanurhastādādadāno mṛtasyāsme kṣatrāya varcase balāya |

paragraphs.text: There art thou, there; and here with noble heroes may we o'ercome all hosts that fight against us.
paragraphs.original: अत्रैव त्वमिह वयं सुवीरा विश्वा स्पृधो अभिमातीर्जयेम
paragraphs.translit: atraiva tvamiha vayaṃ suvīrā viśvā spṛdho abhimātīrjayema

paragraphs.text: 10. Betake thee to the lap of Earth the Mother, of Earth far-spreading, very kind and gracious.
paragraphs.original: उप सर्प मातरं भूमिमेतामुरुव्यचसं पृथिवीं सुशेवाम् ।
paragraphs.translit: upa sarpa mātaraṃ bhūmimetāmuruvyacasaṃ pṛthivīṃ suśevām |

paragraphs.text: Young Dame, wool-soft unto the guerdon giver, may she preserve thee from Destruction's bosom.
paragraphs.original: ऊर्णम्रदा युवतिर्दक्षिणावत एषा त्वा पातु निरृतेरुपस्थात्
paragraphs.translit: ūrṇamradā yuvatirdakṣiṇāvata eṣā tvā pātu nirṛterupasthāt

paragraphs.text: 11. Heave thyself, Earth, nor press thee downward heavily: afford him easy access, gently tending him.
paragraphs.original: उच्छ्वञ्चस्व पृथिवि मा नि बाधथाः सूपायनास्मै भव सूपवञ्चना ।
paragraphs.translit: ucchvañcasva pṛthivi mā ni bādhathāḥ sūpāyanāsmai bhava sūpavañcanā |

paragraphs.text: Cover him, as a mother wraps her skirt about her child, O Earth.
paragraphs.original: माता पुत्रं यथा सिचाभ्येनं भूम ऊर्णुहि
paragraphs.translit: mātā putraṃ yathā sicābhyenaṃ bhūma ūrṇuhi

paragraphs.text: 12. Now let the heaving earth be free from motion: yea,- let a thousand clods remain above him.
paragraphs.original: उच्छ्वञ्चमाना पृथिवी सु तिष्ठतु सहस्रं मित उप हि श्रयन्ताम् ।
paragraphs.translit: ucchvañcamānā pṛthivī su tiṣṭhatu sahasraṃ mita upa hi śrayantām |

paragraphs.text: Be they to him a home distilling fatness, here let them ever be his place of refuge.
paragraphs.original: ते गृहासो घृतश्चुतो भवन्तु विश्वाहास्मै शरणाः सन्त्वत्र
paragraphs.translit: te gṛhāso ghṛtaścuto bhavantu viśvāhāsmai śaraṇāḥ santvatra

paragraphs.text: 13. I stay the earth from thee, while over thee I place this piece of earth. May I be free from injury.
paragraphs.original: उत्ते स्तभ्नामि पृथिवीं त्वत्परीमं लोगं निदधन्मो अहं रिषम् ।
paragraphs.translit: utte stabhnāmi pṛthivīṃ tvatparīmaṃ logaṃ nidadhanmo ahaṃ riṣam |

paragraphs.text: Here let the Fathers keep this pillar firm for thee, and there let Yama make thee an abiding-place.
paragraphs.original: एतां स्थूणां पितरो धारयन्तु तेऽत्रा यमः सादना ते मिनोतु
paragraphs.translit: etāṃ sthūṇāṃ pitaro dhārayantu te'trā yamaḥ sādanā te minotu

paragraphs.text: 14. Even as an arrow's feathers, they have set me on a fitting day.
paragraphs.original: प्रतीचीने मामहनीष्वाः पर्णमिवा दधुः ।
paragraphs.translit: pratīcīne māmahanīṣvāḥ parṇamivā dadhuḥ |

paragraphs.text: The fit word have I caught and held as 'twere a courser with the rein.
paragraphs.original: प्रतीचीं जग्रभा वाचमश्वं रशनया यथा
paragraphs.translit: pratīcīṃ jagrabhā vācamaśvaṃ raśanayā yathā
